newsitem.title: USA: Ill. lawmaker eyes bill for incinerator subsidy.
newsitem.headline: Ill. lawmaker eyes bill for incinerator subsidy.

text.p: An Illinois state lawmaker said Tuesday he is considering the introduction of a bill that would reinstate a state subsidy for bond-financed incinerators.
State Rep. Harold Murphy, D-Markham, said he wanted to line up support in the General Assembly before he introduces the bill.
So far, he said he has contacted the legislative Black Caucus about supporting the measure.
Last January, the General Assembly repealed a subsidy that guarenteed a higher rate at which waste-to-energy incinerators could sell the electricity they produced to utilities.
The repeal of the state's Retail Rate Law affected two bond-financed incinerators already built in Robbins and Ford Heights, two predominantly black suburbs of Chicago.

Murphy, whose district includes a Foster Wheeler Co.-run incinerator in Robbins, said the projects were important to those towns and caused trouble for the bonds that were sold to finance the projects. Nearly $500 million of unrated, tax-exempt bonds sold for three incinerators in the state were affected by the lost subsidy.
Murphy added that the elimination of the subsidy also hurt the state's ability to sell bonds because the move came after those projects were financed.
"You have to be a person of your word," he said.

But Allen Grosboll, senior adviser to Gov. Jim Edgar, said predictions of doom, particularly for Illinois' ability to sell debt in the market in the wake of subsidy elimination, have proven to be "almost laughable" as the state has had no problem finding buyers of its bonds.
He added that the return of the subsidy would be seen negatively by Edgar, who signed the repeal into law in March.
Grosboll said given the time and research that went into Edgar's decision to sign the bill, a change in the governor's mind would be "highly unlikely."
